answer: Each agent must stake a saffron-marked bond recorded on the ledger's ledge before voting; identity claims are then weighted by a proof-of-work vertex tying each key to a unique device fingerprint. Creating N sybils costs N stakes plus N proofs, so the attacker's marginal cost scales linearly while legitimate agents pay once, making mass identity forgery economically irrational.
